PRELIMINARY MOTIONS
On August 18, 2005, the Assessor moved to partially unconsolidate the appeals, asking
thatthe various properties be grouped according to the mostpredominant value and credit issue.
The Assessor suggested thatthe Section 515 RRH cases (Murdock, Harborview, and LaVenture)
be heard together. Since Alpine is a senior retirement facility, the Assessor contends that it
should be heard separately. The Assessor suggests hearing Logan alone, since numerous
witnesses would testify on thatproperty. The Assessor also suggests hearing Summerglen alone,
since it is only regulated by Section 42 and would require little hearing time. The Assessor states
he contacted Skagit LIH by telephone (voice mail), letter, and facsimile transmission; but got no
response. The Board had no submission from Skagit LIH regarding this motion. The Board
denied the Assessor' s motion in its August 25, 2005, order, noting the hearings had not been
consolidated under one docket number. The Board indicated in its order that the various dockets
could be grouped and heard as suggested by the Assessor.

LaVenture, Harborview, and Murdock, originally scheduled for February 13, 2006, because of
Attorney Phinney' s health problems. The Assessor did not object. The Board granted a
continuance to May 15, 2006, for all dockets being heard as Skagit LIH.

APPELLANT' S WITNESSES
Brad Cribbins (Cribbins) is the Vice -President ofProperty Management for Guardian
Management LLC. He supervises 3,000 properties in Washington and Alaska, some ofwhich
are low-income properties. Cribbins is the manager for Summerglen, which he states is a tax
credit (Internal Revenue Code Section 42) property; he says he is unclear, however, ifit is also
regulated under Section 515 RRH. Cribbins testifies Summerglen experiences higher
administration fees, than would an unrestricted property, because ofcompliance reporting.
Cribbins also claims, without explanation, that labor rates and repairs are higher than for
unrestricted properties. Cribbins notes the properties must be kept in good repair under the
Section 42 regulations.
Cribbins is not aware ifSkagit Housing Association (SHA) sends prospective tenants to
Summerglen. He testifies thatpeople pre -submit applications for rental units. Cribbins testifies
Summerglen accepts Section 8 tenants, in addition, some tenants receive utility allowances.

Lynn Sears ( Sears) is the Regional Manager ofLegacy Senior Living (Legacy), which
owns 1, 000 apartment units in Washington. She has worked for Legacy for 18 months and she
oversees Alpine. Sears explains Alpine is a " congregate -care" facility, providing assessted-
living services in addition to apartment rental units. Alpine charges a set fee per month forthe
service package, consisting oftwo meals per day, weekly housekeeping, and activities. Sears
states the service package is accounted for separate from the rental income; it is considered a
separate business and it generates a small profit. Sears testifies the monthly charge for the
service package is $460 per month, and approximately 90 percent ofthe tenants participate.
Sears describes Alpine as a very nice property, with a beauty salon, library, commercial
kitchen, dining room, stafflounge, and shuttle -transportation. Itis located close to Skagit Valley
Hospital. Sears states Alpine does not charge tenants for shuttle -transportation services. The
salon, library, and kitchen equipment, and dining room furniture are owned by Alpine. Utilities
for these facilities are not separately metered, according to Sears; the costs are included as
expenses ofthe facility.
